problem_statement: When out is NULL, fmt_bytes_hex_reverse(char *out, const uint8_t *ptr, size_t n) must return the number of bytes that would have been written, namely 2 * n. When out is not NULL, its observable behaviour is to write the bytes of ptr in reverse order as two-character hex values. A NULL out is currently not handled and leads to failure instead of returning the length.

verification.reason: The problem statement fully specifies the only new behavior the fix introduces: NULL handling for fmt_bytes_hex_reverse returning 2*n. All other test assertions (NULL handling for fmt_byte_hex, fmt_bytes_hex, fmt_hex_bytes; odd-length behavior for fmt_hex_bytes; edge cases for fmt_is_number, fmt_is_digit, fmt_is_upper, fmt_hex_byte) verify pre-existing behavior that the fix does not modify, so they will pass with the existing code regardless of the agent's changes to fmt_bytes_hex_reverse.
